key_insight: TRAMA transfers knowledge from a cheap linear property into a reusable learned search space for optimizing nonlinear mechanical metamaterial behavior.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces expensive simulation calls for energy-absorbing metamaterial design, saving approximately 100 hours per finite-element optimization campaign.
method: Learn a compact design representation using a variational autoencoder.
Incorporate a pre-trained vision transformer and physics-informed augmentations.
Reuse the learned search space to optimize nonlinear, potentially non-differentiable targets.
evidence_signal: For energy-absorption efficiency, TRAMA required 95–98% fewer evaluations than state-of-the-art gradient-free optimization; fabricated designs matched simulated stress–strain curves within 5.3%.
watch_item: Transferability is property-dependent: the learned representation does not generalize equally well to every new target.
paper_title: Efficient Optimization of Mechanical Metamaterials via Transferable Representation Learning
